summary: This note covers how George Lucas, Rick McCallum, and casting director Robin Gurland chose Natalie Portman to play Padmé Amidala in The Phantom Menace. The team auditioned over 200 actresses before selecting the 16-year-old Portman. Lucas was impressed by her earlier performances in The Professional and Beautiful Girls and described the qualities he wanted for the role.
one_line: Casting of Natalie Portman as Padmé Amidala in The Phantom Menace, after an audition of over 200 actresses.
key_facts: George Lucas, Rick McCallum, and casting director Robin Gurland auditioned over 200 actresses for the part of Padmé Amidala.
The team chose 16-year-old actress Natalie Portman to play Padmé Amidala.
According to The Phantom Menace production notes, the role required a young woman who could be believable as the ruler of that planet, but at the same time be vulnerable and open.
Natalie Portman's performance in The Professional (1994) impressed George Lucas.
Natalie Portman's performance in Beautiful Girls (1996) impressed George Lucas.
George Lucas said he was looking for someone who was young, strong, along the lines of Leia.
George Lucas said Natalie Portman embodied all those traits and more.
